title: The Seven Storey Mountain (1948)
hookLine: his memoir, named from Dante, becomes a bestseller he wrote in a cell

lines: A MONK WHO CAME TO DISAPPEAR.
WRITE THE STORY OF YOUR LIFE.
cards: A man walks into a monastery to disappear. He gives up his name, his money, his career as a writer. He speaks with his hands.
Then his abbot comes to him and says: I'd like you to write the story of your life. Seven years after he rang the gate bell, that story is sitting in bookstore windows.
The man who came to be forgotten is about to become very hard to forget. Today: the book that made a hidden monk well-known.

teach.b: First, the order to write. Merton had thought he'd have to give up writing to be a monk. His abbot, Dom Frederic Dunne, saw it differently and asked him to keep going.
So in the middle of the Trappist day, between the night office and the fields, Merton wrote his autobiography. Second, the title. The Seven Storey Mountain comes from Dante's Divine Comedy.
In the poem's second part, Purgatory is a great mountain with seven levels, one for each of the seven deadly sins, and souls climb it, healed of each one on the way up to God.
Merton saw his own life that way: not a straight line, but a long, hard climb out of pride and drifting, one ledge at a time. Third, the surprise.
The book came out in 1948 and became a bestseller. A monk who had vowed to stay put in one monastery, and who barely spoke, suddenly had readers he would never meet.
Fourth, the older Merton. Years later he said the book was too harsh about the world he'd left, too sure of itself. He didn't take it back.
He kept writing, and kept changing. The title holds that, too. A mountain isn't climbed in one step.
A life of faith is a story still being told, and the teller is allowed to grow.

how: Many Catholics find their way to Merton through The Seven Storey Mountain, and writing a spiritual autobiography or journal is a practice some spiritual directors suggest for noticing where God has been at work.

games.q: you're the abbot. a gifted young monk thinks he must stop writing to be holy. what do you tell him?
o: yes, give it up for good
write the story of your life
games.why: Dom Frederic Dunne encouraged him to write. the book became The Seven Storey Mountain, and a bestseller.

practice: With a pen or your phone's notes, let your life so far come to mind as a climb, not a verdict. Write three unpolished lines nobody else has to read: where you started, one ledge where something changed, where you are now.
If you pray, you can hold them up to God without explaining.

wordCard.voice: Purgatory. Dante's seven-level mountain that gave Merton's 1948 memoir its name and its picture of a soul climbing one level at a time. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the mountain is a story. One bad day is a ledge, not the end. See you tomorrow.
